paragraphs.text: Food is an artifact type and predefined token introduced in Throne of Eldraine .

Food tokens have “ , , Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life.” Although it does appear in the type line of some cards, the type mostly appears on tokens . R&D made food tokens because they realized fairy tales were overrun with food references and it would allow them to design a lot of fun cards.

Food is the third major predefined token type after Clue and Treasure , which have fairly clear payoffs of card advantage and mana acceleration respectively. Food, being life gain, has its greatest impact when one is behind but does little to win a game. The associated mana cost, like with Clues, makes it clunky to rely on to survive as every mana spent to gain life is not spent reversing one's position. Hence, it can be added to cards without adding significant mana, making them attractive options for secondary uses like artifact or sacrifice synergies. That said, the potential for poor gameplay experiences is one R&D is cognizant to avoid, limiting the direct application of simple "create a food".

Since the Food type does not inherently grant the ability possessed by the predefined Food token, it is possible for cards with the Food type to not have that ability. However, for thematic reasons, all of these artifacts also have some form of " , , Sacrifice this artifact: You gain 3 life." As a tap ability, all food creatures are subject to summoning sickness , delaying the ability. Notable deviations from the standard ability include the following:
Candy Trail 's ability also draws a card, as it is meant to represent a combination of the standard Food and Clue abilities. Bagel and Schmear does also despite not being a Clue.

Syr Ginger, the Meal Ender 's ability gains life equal to her power , which is 3 by default but is likely to change from her own ability. Ginger, Queen of Sweets also gains life equal to her power, but insofar as both are set at 6.

Three Bowls of Porridge has a modal ability where the standard Food ability is one option among three. As a consequence of the templating, the sacrificing occurs during the resolution of the ability when this mode is chosen, not as a cost of activation like with the standard Food ability.

Vegetation Abomination makes its controller roll a six-sided die to determine how much life they will gain. To compensate for being weaker a third of the time, as well as being a creature, it does not require a mana cost.
Dimension X Pizzasaur also causes the opponent to lose 3 life.

Pizza Face, Gastromancer has a supersized food ability that costs to gain 15 life, the same mana-to-life ratio. Given the mana cost the ability is almost trinket text , so it also creates a conventional Food token.
Everything Pizza has its ability cost , of which gaining 3 life is one of the five colored effects.
Food tokens returned as a one-off in Commander 2021 on Gyome, Master Chef , and got six new producers in Modern Horizons 2 . Food was not considered deciduous until Streets of New Capenna .

In The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth and Wilds of Eldraine , Food tokens are a larger mechanical draft theme. R&D noted a problematic gameplay issue in the original Eldraine set that the payoffs for making Food tended toward shrinking the board or deterring attacking, which compounded with how natural life gain ability of Food also slows the game. Hence, the secondary uses of Food in these newer sets tended towards more proactive play.
Bloomburrow introduced Forage , a mechanical cost that includes the sacrifice of Food, serving as the backbone of the Squirrels archetype.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles has a focus on pizza as emblematic of its New York teenager aesthetic, but the world also includes multiple mutated creatures that are sentient foodstuffs. The food cards, hence, have greater utility beyond the gaining of life.
Tokens marked with are created by Acorn cards.
